region.text: Sindh, governed by Umar bin Abdul Aziz al-Habbari for the Abbasids from 854

ledger.note: 861: Umar al-Habbari makes Sindh independent. 'Umar's request to be formally appointed governor was granted in 854' (al-Ya'qubi); 'Umar became independent after al-Mutawakkil's death in 861, but continued to read the Friday prayers in the name of the Abbasid caliph.' Cliopatria starts the row in 860.

883: Mansura is made the capital. 'Mansura was designated their capital in 883' (the Mansura page gives the city as the Sindh capital 'from the year 750 AD to 1006 AD'; its coins are 'Amirs of Sind, c. 870-1030').

1025: Mahmud of Ghazni invades Mansura. The Diwan-i Farruhi dates 'Mahmud of Ghazni's invasion (1025 AD) of Mansura, the erstwhile capital of Sindh'; the infobox and the Habbari page put the conquest in 1026.

1026: Mansura falls. The state was 'conquered by the Ghaznavids in 1026'; Mahmud 'went on to destroy the old Habbari capital of Mansura' and annexed the region, ending Arab rule of Sindh. The Ghaznavid page's Somnath raid is also dated 1026.

1026: the Habbari emirate ends at Mansura. The page's reign table ends with Manbi in 1010 and its last ruler Khafif ('may have converted to Isma'ili Islam') is undated there; the Soomra page lists Khafif 1010-1026 and 'Soomra dynasty begins: 1026', 'Tributary of the Ghaznavids (1026-1030)'. The page's own end dates disagree: infobox header 1011, lead 'from 854 to 1024', conquest 1026.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Multan
belligerents: Emirate of Multan (Banu Munabih / Ismaili rulers)
wars.outcome: Multan taken by Mahmud of Ghazni: '1005' on the Habbari page, '1006' on the Ghaznavid page ('in 1006 the neighbouring Emirate of Multan'); Multan was never Habbari land.
wars.note: The Habbari page: 'Multan was ruled by the Banu Munabih, not the Habbaris'. Listed because it fixes the Habbari northern limit; no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Mansura
wars.outcome: Mansura sacked and the Habbari emirate ended in 1026; the Soomras follow as Ghaznavid tributaries (1026-1030).
wars.note: The Ghaznavid page is silent on this campaign; the Soomra page dates the invasion 1025; the Mansura page says only 'Mansura was sacked by the forces of Mahmud of Ghazni'.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line: the realm is described as the land 'between the Arabian Sea and Aror'. The coast is the firm edge; the northern limit toward Multan and Uch, and the Makran and Khuzdar edges, are soft.

notes:
HABBARI DYNASTY (sa-03-e). 5 pages opened (the budget for 11 Cliopatria shapes), which also serve the Soomra dossier.

SPLIT: the Cliopatria row 'Sind-Habbari Dynasty' (860-1201) is two states. The Habbari page ends the dynasty 'from 854 to 1024' (lead), '854-1011' (header) and with the Ghaznavid conquest of Mansura in 1026; the Soomra page's infobox starts 'Soomra dynasty begins: 1026'. This dossier reviews the shapes of 860-1026; the Soomra dossier (soomra-dynasty, new) reviews 1027-1201 and extends to 1351. If the orchestrator prefers one state, the Habbari to Soomra change is a rename (the Soomra table lists Khafif 1010-1026 as its first ruler) and the two files can be merged under this slug.

Start year: 861 (independence after al-Mutawakkil's death) rather than 854 (governor's appointment) or Cliopatria's 860; the page's own dates are 854/855.

Realm: the page puts the realm 'between the Arabian Sea and Aror' plus Khuzdar until the late 9th century (when Mughira bin Ahmad moved the capital to Kijkanan); Multan belonged to the Banu Munabih and Makran to the Banu Ma'dan. Cliopatria's shape was therefore corrected to the province of Sindh. Khuzdar and Turan are not drawn (Cliopatria's bbox barely touches Khuzdar); the page gives no year for its loss.

Counterparts needing dossiers: Emirate of Multan (Banu Munabih, then Ismaili / Qarmatian rulers until Muhammad of Ghor took Multan in 1175; the Ghaznavid page has it conquered in 1006); the Ghaznavid dossier should carry the Soomra tribute 1026-1030.
Gazetteer names needed: Mansura (Brahmanabad) as a place (the gazetteer has only El Mansura in Egypt; coordinates are in the capital entry), Aror.
Disagreements: Multan conquered 1005 (Habbari page) vs 1006 (Ghaznavid page); Umar's reign 854-883 vs 855-884; end 1011/1024/1026; the Mansura page says earthquake of 893 and capital 'from 750 to 1006'.
